supersedes: The operative belief that CH-11 and CH-13 were blocked by the RC-C5 hard gate. PORTFOLIO_GOVERNANCE_DOCTRINE §2 (NOT_RECORDED) and §6 (BIFURCATED) are historical evidence and are NOT rewritten; this ruling is recorded forward.
question: Does the historical C4 -> RC-C5 authorization gate transfer to CH-11, CH-13 or CH-14, which inherited obligations chartered under RC-C5?
canonicalInterpretation: The gate governed the RC-C4 -> RC-C5 chapter/deployment transition.
Obligation provenance is NOT authorization inheritance.
The later BIFURCATED doctrine prevents retroactive extension.
Section 12 Rich Content remains governed by its own RIC staging.
RIC-C5 must never be conflated with RC-C5.
Successor chapters inherit the OBLIGATIONS, not an obsolete chapter transition gate, unless a gate was explicitly preserved.

evidenceRecovered.frozenGateText: C5 remains CLOSED until C4 is implemented, locally certified, pushed as authorized, deployed, observed end-to-end on the LIVE site, live defects resolved, and founder declares C4 certified/closed. C4 LOCAL CERTIFICATION != C5 AUTHORIZATION.

Any later reader equating them would produce a confidently wrong mapping. The belief that CH-13's 26 obligations sat behind the RC-C5 hard gate was that mapping.
